```{r libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(splicelogic)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
library(here)
library(plyxp)
devtools::load_all(here("../splicelogic"))
```

## Load bambu output

`bambu_discovery.rds` is the exon-by-transcript `GRangesList` from bambu's
discovery run (novel plus annotated transcripts); `bambu_quant_se.rds` is the
matching quantification `SummarizedExperiment`.

```{r setup_bambu, message=FALSE}
bdisc    <- readRDS(here("workflows", "data", "bambu_discovery.rds"))
se_bambu <- readRDS(here("workflows", "data", "bambu_quant_se.rds"))
bdisc
```

## Transcript annotation (condition, CPM, direction)

Condition and donor live only in the sample names; `ctrl` -> WT and `exp` -> KD
to match the satuRn workflow. For each transcript we take the mean CPM in each
group and the `log2(WT / KD)` fold change, whose sign gives the direction.

```{r condition_cpm}
cn <- colnames(se_bambu)
colData(se_bambu)$condition <- factor(
  ifelse(grepl("_ctrl", cn), "WT", "KD"), levels = c("KD", "WT")
)
colData(se_bambu)$donor <- sub("-0008.*$", "", cn)
table(colData(se_bambu)$donor, colData(se_bambu)$condition)

cpm   <- assay(se_bambu, "CPM")
is_wt <- colData(se_bambu)$condition == "WT"

rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_WT <- rowMeans(cpm[,  is_wt, drop = FALSE])
rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_KD <- rowMeans(cpm[, !is_wt, drop = FALSE])
rowData(se_bambu)$lfc_WT_vs_KD <- log2((rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_WT + 1) /
                                       (rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_KD + 1))
rowData(se_bambu)$direction <- ifelse(
  rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_WT > rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_KD, "up_in_WT",
  ifelse(rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_WT < rowData(se_bambu)$cpm_KD, "up_in_KD", "tie")
)

# most `tie` rows are transcripts at zero in both groups
table(rowData(se_bambu)$direction)
table(rowData(se_bambu)$direction[rowMeans(cpm) > 1])
```

A quick look at the novel genes' expression, to see how much signal there is.

```{r explore_novel, message=FALSE}
xp <- se_bambu |> new_plyxp()
xp_novel <- xp |>
  filter(rows(novelGene)) |>
  mutate(rows(mean_cpm = rowMeans(.assays_asis$CPM)))
nrow(xp_novel)

table(cut(log10(rowData(xp_novel)$mean_cpm), -3:3))
hist(log10(rowData(xp_novel)$mean_cpm))
```

### Expression filter

Keep transcripts with raw count >= 10 in at least
6 samples. Applied before building the exon
object so both the novel (`up`) and annotated (`down`) partitions are filtered.

```{r expression_filter}
# transcripts per type, before and after the filter
count_tx_type <- \(se) table(
  tx_type = ifelse(rowData(se)$novelTranscript, "novel", "annotated")
)
n_before <- count_tx_type(se_bambu)

min_count   <- 10
min_samples <- 6
keep_counts <- rowSums(assay(se_bambu, "counts") >= min_count) >= min_samples
se_bambu    <- se_bambu[keep_counts, ]
dim(se_bambu)

n_after <- count_tx_type(se_bambu)
```

```{r plot_filter_counts, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
filter_counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "unfiltered" = as.data.frame(n_before, responseName = "n"),
  "filtered"   = as.data.frame(n_after,  responseName = "n"),
  .id = "stage"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = c("unfiltered", "filtered"))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tx_type) |>
  # the filtered bar also shows the share retained
  dplyr::mutate(label = ifelse(
    stage == "filtered",
    sprintf("%s\n(%.1f%%)", scales::comma(n), 100 * n / max(n)),
    scales::comma(n)
  ))

ggplot(filter_counts, aes(x = tx_type, y = n, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.9, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "unfiltered" = "#B0CFFF",  # light blue
    "filtered"   = "#3A86FF"   # darker blue
  )) +
  # log scale from 1: the annotated set is ~100x the novel set, so on a
  # linear axis the novel bars would be slivers. Every decade is labelled.
  scale_y_log10(breaks = 10^(0:6), minor_breaks = NULL,
                labels = scales::comma, limits = c(1, NA),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Transcripts before and after the expression filter",
       subtitle = sprintf("Filter: raw count ≥ %d in at least %d of %d samples",
                          min_count, min_samples, ncol(se_bambu)),
       x = NULL, y = "log(Number of Transcripts)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Flat exon GRanges

A flat `GRanges`, one range per exon, with the transcript-level annotation
joined on. This is the exon object the splicelogic `find_*()` and `plot_*()`
functions take.

```{r build_exons}
exons <- unlist(bdisc, use.names = TRUE)
exons$tx_id <- names(exons)

# bdisc carries every discovered transcript; keep only those retained by the
# expression filter on se_bambu, so the match below is complete.
rd    <- rowData(se_bambu)
exons <- exons[exons$tx_id %in% rd$TXNAME]
i     <- match(exons$tx_id, rd$TXNAME)
stopifnot(!anyNA(i))

cols    <- c("GENEID", "novelGene", "novelTranscript", "txClassDescription",
             "NDR", "readCount", "relReadCount",
             "cpm_WT", "cpm_KD", "lfc_WT_vs_KD", "direction")
tx_info <- rd[, cols]
tx_info$mean_cpm <- rowMeans(assay(se_bambu, "CPM"))
tx_info$n_det    <- rowSums(assay(se_bambu, "counts") > 0)

mcols(exons) <- cbind(mcols(exons), tx_info[i, ])
names(mcols(exons))[names(mcols(exons)) == "GENEID"] <- "gene_id"

# bambu exons carry no exon_id. Build one from gene + coordinates (per the
# splicelogic vignette), so the same exon gets the same id in every transcript
# that contains it.
exons$exon_id <- paste0(exons$gene_id, ":",
                        start(exons), "-", end(exons))
```

### Novel transcript counts

The comparison keeps novel transcripts at **annotated** loci (so there is an
annotated partner to compare against) and drops novel transcripts at entirely
new loci.

```{r novel_counts}
count_gr <- function(gr, label) {
  data.frame(set   = label,
             exons = length(gr),
             tx    = length(unique(gr$tx_id)),
             genes = length(unique(gr$gene_id)))
}

rbind(
  count_gr(exons, "all (extended annotation)"),
  count_gr(exons[exons$novelTranscript],  "novel transcripts"),
  count_gr(exons[!exons$novelTranscript], "annotated transcripts"),
  count_gr(exons[exons$novelTranscript &  exons$novelGene], "  novel tx, NEW locus (drop)"),
  count_gr(exons[exons$novelTranscript & !exons$novelGene], "  novel tx, annotated gene (keep)")
) |> print(row.names = FALSE)
```

## Splice event detection with splicelogic

The two partitions are defined explicitly (no DTU test): the **up** set is the
novel transcripts at annotated loci, the **down** (reference) set is the
annotated transcripts. `prepare_exons_by_partition()` assigns `estimate = +1`
to up and `-1` to down.

```{r find_events}
up   <- exons |> dplyr::filter(!novelGene, novelTranscript)
down <- exons |> dplyr::filter(!novelGene, !novelTranscript)

# genes present in both partitions are the ones with a comparison to make
length(intersect(unique(up$gene_id), unique(down$gene_id)))

sl_exons <- prepare_exons_by_partition(up, down) |>
  preprocess(coef_col = "estimate")

events_bambu <- find_all_events(sl_exons)
```

### Collapse redundant events

An exon paired with several partner transcripts is reported once per partner,
as repeated rows with the same range. Collapsing those per event type shows how
much of the raw event count is that redundancy. Rows are collapsed only for the
same exon (gene, chromosome, start, end, strand) and the same event type, as in
the other workflows.

```{r collapse_redundant_events}
# define a helper function
my_paste <- \(x) paste(unique(x), collapse = ",")

# the exon is identified by `exon_key` (gene, chromosome, start, end and
# strand), built as in the vignette's recipe for an exon id, rather than by
# `exon_id`: the annotation can give the same exon more than one id
collapsed_events <- events_bambu |>
  dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
  plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
    n           = plyranges::n(),
    exon_id     = my_paste(exon_id),
    tx_id       = my_paste(tx_id),
    exon_rank   = my_paste(exon_rank),
    event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id)
  )
```

```{r barplot_event_types}
event_counts <- events_bambu |>
  as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::count(event_type, name = "count")

collapsed_event_counts <- collapsed_events |>
  as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::count(event_type, name = "count")

# combine both count tables into one, labelled by source
counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "All events" = event_counts,
  "Collapsed events" = collapsed_event_counts,
  .id = "set"
)

# event types from most to fewest events
counts$event_type <- factor(
  counts$event_type,
  levels = event_counts$event_type[order(-event_counts$count)]
)

ggplot(counts, aes(x = event_type, y = count, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "All events" = "#B0CFFF",       # light blue
    "Collapsed events" = "#3A86FF"  # darker blue
  )) +
  labs(title = "Novel-transcript splice event counts",
       x = "Event Type", y = "Count", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r pie_collapsed_event_types, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
# event types in the package's order, with the package's colours, so each type
# matches its colour in plot_transcripts()
type_colors <- event_palette()
type_order  <- names(type_colors)

pie_counts <- collapsed_event_counts |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    event_type = factor(event_type, levels = type_order),
    pct        = 100 * count / sum(count),
    # slices under 5% are too thin to label; the legend carries them
    label      = ifelse(pct >= 5,
                        sprintf("%s\n%.1f%%", toupper(event_type), pct), "")
  )

legend_labels <- with(pie_counts, setNames(
  sprintf("%s  %d (%.1f%%)", toupper(event_type), count, pct),
  event_type
))

ggplot(pie_counts, aes(x = 1, y = count, fill = event_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # labels just outside the pie, at each slice's midpoint
  geom_text(aes(x = 1.75, label = label, group = event_type),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.2, lineheight = 0.9, colour = "grey20") +
  # clockwise from 12 o'clock, in the same order as the legend
  coord_polar(theta = "y", direction = -1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = type_colors, labels = legend_labels) +
  labs(title = "Collapsed novel-transcript events by type",
       subtitle = sprintf("n = %s", scales::comma(sum(pie_counts$count))),
       fill = NULL) +
  theme_void()
```

## Per-transcript annotation for the plots

One label per transcript (novel status, then the direction and the two group
means) and a matching `log2(WT / KD)` value used to draw the LFC strip beside
each transcript.

```{r plot_annotation}
# Pulled into a plain data.frame and read with with(): repeating `rd$` inside
# one call makes the console's `$` completion eat the paste.
d <- as.data.frame(rd[, c("TXNAME", "novelTranscript",
                          "cpm_WT", "cpm_KD", "lfc_WT_vs_KD")])

# novel/annot status, plus the direction and group means. A direction on two
# near-zero means is rounding noise, not a change, so those read "n.d.".
tx_annot <- with(d, paste0(
  ifelse(novelTranscript, "novel", "annot"), " | ",
  ifelse(cpm_WT + cpm_KD < 0.1, "n.d.",
         sprintf("log2 %+.2f  (WT %.2f / KD %.2f)", lfc_WT_vs_KD, cpm_WT, cpm_KD))
))
names(tx_annot) <- d[["TXNAME"]]

# log2(WT/KD) for the LFC strip: NA (no bar) where both groups are near zero.
tx_lfc <- with(d, ifelse(cpm_WT + cpm_KD < 0.1, NA_real_, lfc_WT_vs_KD))
names(tx_lfc) <- d[["TXNAME"]]

# one shared scale so bar lengths mean the same thing on every page
lfc_max <- quantile(abs(tx_lfc), 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Plotting helpers

Two small helpers that the package does not provide: a multi-page PDF writer,
and a per-gene layout that places `plot_transcripts()` next to the companion
`plot_transcript_lfc()` strip (the package draws them as separate plots; here
`patchwork` composes them so they share row order and y limits).

```{r plot_helpers}
fig_dir <- here("workflows", "figures")
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# write a list of plots to one multi-page PDF, one plot per page
write_pdf <- function(plots, file, width = 10, height = 6) {
  grDevices::pdf(file, width = width, height = height, onefile = TRUE)
  on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  for (nm in names(plots)) print(plots[[nm]])
  invisible(file)
}

# plot_transcripts() + plot_transcript_lfc() side by side, one pair per gene
plot_gene_with_lfc <- function(events, exons, tx_lfc, lfc_max = NULL,
                               tx_annot = NULL, lfc_ends = c("KD", "WT"),
                               widths = c(5, 1.2), ...) {
  genes <- unique(as.character(events$gene_id))
  plots <- lapply(stats::setNames(genes, genes), function(g) {
    ev <- events[as.character(events$gene_id) == g]
    tryCatch({
      p <- plot_transcripts(ev, exons, title = g, tx_annot = tx_annot, ...)
      q <- plot_transcript_lfc(ev, tx_lfc, lfc_max = lfc_max,
                               lfc_ends = lfc_ends)
      patchwork::wrap_plots(p, q, widths = widths)
    }, error = function(e) {
      warning("Skipping ", g, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
      NULL
    })
  })
  Filter(Negate(is.null), plots)
}
```

## Events for one gene

`exons` is already the flat `GRanges` the package plotting functions take (one
range per exon with a `tx_id` column), so it is passed directly.

```{r plot_one_gene, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
gene_of_interest <- unique(as.character(events_bambu$gene_id))[10]
events_for_gene  <- events_bambu[events_bambu$gene_id == gene_of_interest]

p <- plot_transcripts(events_for_gene, exons, title = gene_of_interest,
                      tx_annot = tx_annot)
q <- plot_transcript_lfc(events_for_gene, tx_lfc, lfc_max = lfc_max,
                         lfc_ends = c("KD", "WT"))
patchwork::wrap_plots(p, q, widths = c(5, 1.2))
```

## All events, one page per gene (with the LFC strip)

```{r plot_by_gene, eval=FALSE}
gene_plots <- plot_gene_with_lfc(
  events_bambu, exons,
  tx_annot = tx_annot, tx_lfc = tx_lfc, lfc_max = lfc_max
)
length(gene_plots)

write_pdf(gene_plots, file.path(fig_dir, "events_by_gene_bambu.pdf"))
```

## All events, one page per transcript pair

`plot_transcripts_by_pair()` splits on the transcript pair internally, so
`events_bambu` works directly.

```{r plot_by_pair, eval=FALSE}
pair_plots <- plot_transcripts_by_pair(events_bambu, exons)
length(pair_plots)

write_pdf(pair_plots, file.path(fig_dir, "events_by_pair_bambu.pdf"), height = 3)
```

## Novel transcripts split by direction

Plot the novel transcripts separately by the direction of their WT/KD change.
In each event row the novel transcript is the one from the `up` partition
(`estimate > 0`): `tx_id` when the row's own estimate is positive, otherwise its
partner `event_tx_id`.

```{r novel_by_direction}
ev <- as.data.frame(S4Vectors::mcols(events_bambu)[, c("tx_id", "event_tx_id",
                                                       "estimate", "gene_id")])
novel_tx  <- with(ev, ifelse(estimate > 0, as.character(tx_id),
                             as.character(event_tx_id)))
novel_lfc <- unname(tx_lfc[novel_tx])   # NA when the novel transcript is n.d.

# which() drops the NA rows, so n.d. novel transcripts are in neither set
events_novel_kd <- events_bambu[which(novel_lfc < 0)]
events_novel_wt <- events_bambu[which(novel_lfc > 0)]

n_genes <- function(keep) length(unique(ev[["gene_id"]][keep]))
data.frame(
  set    = c("all events", "novel tx higher in KD (< 0)",
             "novel tx higher in WT (> 0)", "novel tx n.d. (not plotted)"),
  events = c(nrow(ev), sum(novel_lfc < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
             sum(novel_lfc > 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(is.na(novel_lfc))),
  genes  = c(n_genes(TRUE), n_genes(which(novel_lfc < 0)),
             n_genes(which(novel_lfc > 0)), n_genes(is.na(novel_lfc)))
)

novel_sets <- list(novel_higher_in_KD = events_novel_kd,
                   novel_higher_in_WT = events_novel_wt)
```

A gene with novel transcripts in both directions appears in both PDFs, each
page showing only the novel transcripts of that direction and their partners.

```{r plot_novel_by_direction, eval=FALSE}
for (set in names(novel_sets)) {
  set_plots <- plot_gene_with_lfc(
    novel_sets[[set]], exons,
    tx_annot = tx_annot, tx_lfc = tx_lfc, lfc_max = lfc_max
  )
  set_file <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("events_", set, "_bambu.pdf"))
  write_pdf(set_plots, set_file)
  message(set, ": ", length(set_plots), " pages written to ", set_file)
}
```

## Splice-site logos for the novel-transcript events

Every event exon is a real spliced exon, so its flanking splice sites should be
the canonical ones: the **3' acceptor** (`...AG |` exon) in the region
**upstream** of the exon, and the **5' donor** (exon `| GU...`) **downstream**.
This is a sanity check that the novel-transcript events sit at genuine splice
sites. A first exon has no acceptor (the bases before it are the transcription
start) and a last exon no donor (the transcription end), so each side only uses
the exons that actually have that splice site. Many novel events sit on
terminal exons: most A5SS exons are first exons and most A3SS exons last ones.
ATSS and ATES events are included on the same rule: an ATSS exon is a first
exon, so only its donor is used, and an ATES exon a last exon, so only its
acceptor.

```{r logo_helpers, message=FALSE}
source(here("workflows/helper.R"))
```

```{r novel_splice_logo, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.2}
# Restrict to the standard chromosomes: the bambu object carries hundreds of
# _fix/_alt scaffolds that are not all in the BSgenome, which otherwise triggers
# a noisy seqinfo-merge warning (and errors for exons on absent scaffolds).
# pruning.mode = "coarse" drops ranges on non-standard seqlevels.
standard_chr <- function(gr) {
  gr <- GenomeInfoDb::keepStandardChromosomes(gr, pruning.mode = "coarse")
  GenomeInfoDb::seqlevels(gr) <- GenomeInfoDb::seqlevelsInUse(gr)
  gr
}

# every event type, ATSS and ATES included: the first/last-exon rule below
# keeps only the donor of an ATSS exon and the acceptor of an ATES exon
splice_events <- standard_chr(events_bambu)

# each event row describes the transcript that contains the exon: novel (the
# up partition) or annotated (down). The annotated event exons are the SE
# exons and one side of each MXE pair; everything else is novel.
is_novel <- splice_events$novelTranscript

# One 1-bp range per distinct splice site: the first base of an exon marks its
# acceptor, the last base its donor (strand-aware). Flanking these gives the
# same intronic bases as flanking the whole exon, and a boundary shared by
# several transcripts counts once. Acceptors come from exons that are not
# first, donors from exons that are not last (bambu's exon_endRank is 1 on the
# last exon).
acceptor_sites <- function(gr) {
  gr <- GenomicRanges::granges(gr[gr$exon_rank > 1])
  unique(GenomicRanges::resize(gr, 1, fix = "start"))
}
donor_sites <- function(gr) {
  gr <- GenomicRanges::granges(gr[gr$exon_endRank > 1])
  unique(GenomicRanges::resize(gr, 1, fix = "end"))
}

# 10 bp into the intron on each side (exon_bases = 0, so purely intronic):
# the upstream logo should end in AG, the downstream logo should start with GU.
splice_site_mats <- function(gr) {
  acc <- slFlankLogoMatrices(acceptor_sites(gr), genome = "hg38",
                             width = 10, exon_bases = 0)
  don <- slFlankLogoMatrices(donor_sites(gr), genome = "hg38",
                             width = 10, exon_bases = 0)
  structure(list(upstream = acc$upstream, downstream = don$downstream),
            width = 10, exon_bases = 0,
            n_sites = c(upstream   = attr(acc, "n_exons"),
                        downstream = attr(don, "n_exons")))
}

plot_splice_site_logo <- function(mats, title) {
  n <- attr(mats, "n_sites")
  slPlotFlankLogo(mats, method = "bits", titles = c(
    upstream   = sprintf("Upstream: 3' splice site (acceptor), n = %d",
                         n[["upstream"]]),
    downstream = sprintf("Downstream: 5' splice site (donor), n = %d",
                         n[["downstream"]])
  )) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title   = title,
      caption = paste("distinct sites; acceptors from non-first exons,",
                      "donors from non-last exons")
    )
}

novel_logo <- splice_site_mats(splice_events[is_novel])
plot_splice_site_logo(novel_logo, "Event exons in novel transcripts")
```

As a reference, every exon of the annotated transcripts (the `down`
partition), not only the annotated event exons, which are just the SE exons and
one side of each MXE pair. These are GENCODE exons, so they should be almost
entirely canonical.

```{r annotated_splice_logo, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.2}
annotated_exons <- standard_chr(down)
annotated_logo  <- splice_site_mats(annotated_exons)
plot_splice_site_logo(annotated_logo, "All exons of annotated transcripts")
```

### Non-canonical splice sites

To find the events that break the pattern, take the 2 intronic bases
immediately flanking each exon — strand-aware, via `plyranges::flank_*()` — and
read them with `get_seq()`. The acceptor (upstream) should be `AG`, the donor
(downstream) `GU`. Anything else is flagged. As for the logos, a first exon has
no acceptor and a last exon no donor; those are recorded as `NA` and not
checked.

```{r splice_dinucleotides, message=FALSE}
# one row per distinct exon within each set, so an exon paired with several
# partners is not counted repeatedly
ex_once <- c(slUniqueExons(splice_events[is_novel]),
             slUniqueExons(splice_events[!is_novel]))
# an exon of a single-exon transcript has no splice site to check
ex_once <- ex_once[ex_once$exon_rank > 1 | ex_once$exon_endRank > 1]

# 2 bp immediately 5' (acceptor) and 3' (donor) of each exon, in transcription
# order; get_seq() reverse-complements minus-strand ranges automatically
acceptor <- ex_once |> plyranges::flank_upstream(width = 2)
donor    <- ex_once |> plyranges::flank_downstream(width = 2)

# NA where the exon has no such site: no acceptor before a first exon, no
# donor after a last one
ex_once$acceptor <- ifelse(
  ex_once$exon_rank > 1,
  as.character(get_seq(acceptor, "hg38", as_rna = TRUE)), NA
)
ex_once$donor <- ifelse(
  ex_once$exon_endRank > 1,
  as.character(get_seq(donor, "hg38", as_rna = TRUE)), NA
)
ex_once$canonical <- (is.na(ex_once$acceptor) | ex_once$acceptor == "AG") &
                     (is.na(ex_once$donor)    | ex_once$donor    == "GU")

# how many follow the canonical AG/GU pattern
table(canonical = ex_once$canonical)
table(acceptor = ex_once$acceptor)
table(donor = ex_once$donor)
table(novel = ex_once$novelTranscript, canonical = ex_once$canonical)
```

The comparison below counts splice sites rather than exons, in two sets: the
splice sites of the novel event exons (`splice_events`, every event type),
against every splice site of the annotated transcripts (`down`) as the
reference. Each distinct site counts once per set, with the same first/last-exon
rule as above, so an ATSS exon contributes only its donor and an ATES exon only
its acceptor.

```{r canonical_by_set, message=FALSE}
# acceptor (AG) and donor (GU) dinucleotide of every distinct splice site
site_canonical <- function(gr) {
  read2 <- function(sites, flank) {
    if (length(sites) == 0L) return(character(0))
    as.character(get_seq(flank(sites, width = 2), "hg38", as_rna = TRUE))
  }
  acc <- read2(acceptor_sites(gr), plyranges::flank_upstream)
  don <- read2(donor_sites(gr),    plyranges::flank_downstream)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(site = "acceptor", seq = acc, canonical = acc == "AG"),
    tibble::tibble(site = "donor",    seq = don, canonical = don == "GU")
  )
}

novel_events <- splice_events[is_novel]

site_sets <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "annotated transcripts" = site_canonical(annotated_exons),
  "novel event exons"     = site_canonical(novel_events),
  .id = "set"
)

site_sets |>
  dplyr::count(set, site, canonical) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = canonical, values_from = n,
                     values_fill = 0L, names_prefix = "canonical_")

# the novel event sites per event type: ATSS adds only donors, ATES only
# acceptors (a site shared by two event types is listed under both)
split(novel_events, novel_events$event_type) |>
  lapply(site_canonical) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "event_type") |>
  dplyr::count(event_type, site, canonical) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = canonical, values_from = n,
                     values_fill = 0L, names_prefix = "canonical_")

canon_p <- fisher.test(table(site_sets$set, site_sets$canonical))$p.value
canon_p
```

```{r plot_canonical_by_set, fig.width=7, fig.height=3}
canon_counts <- site_sets |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    set  = factor(set, levels = c("annotated transcripts",
                                  "novel event exons")),
    site = factor(ifelse(canonical, "canonical (AG/GU)", "non-canonical"),
                  levels = c("non-canonical", "canonical (AG/GU)"))
  ) |>
  dplyr::count(set, site) |>
  # keep zero counts, so a set with no non-canonical sites still gets a label
  tidyr::complete(set, site, fill = list(n = 0L)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(set) |>
  dplyr::mutate(frac  = n / sum(n),
                label = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", scales::comma(n), 100 * frac),
                set   = sprintf("%s\n(n = %s)", set, scales::comma(sum(n)))) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  # annotated at the bottom, novel event exons on top
  dplyr::mutate(set = factor(set, levels = unique(set)))

ggplot(canon_counts, aes(x = frac, y = set, fill = site)) +
  # non-canonical share on the left
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.6) +
  # non-canonical count just right of its segment, canonical at the bar's end
  geom_text(data = \(d) dplyr::filter(d, site == "non-canonical"),
            aes(label = label), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.01,
            size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_text(data = \(d) dplyr::filter(d, site == "canonical (AG/GU)"),
            aes(x = 0.99, label = label), hjust = 1,
            size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("non-canonical"     = "#3A86FF",
                               "canonical (AG/GU)" = "grey85")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Canonical splice sites, novel event exons vs annotated",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0("distinct splice sites, ATSS donors and ATES ",
                                 "acceptors included\nFisher's exact test p = %.2g"),
                          canon_p),
       x = "Share of splice sites", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        # room for the "100%" axis label at the right edge
        plot.margin = margin(5.5, 14, 5.5, 5.5))
```

The novel event exons on their own, counted as exons: an exon is canonical when
every splice site it has is (so an ATSS exon is judged on its donor, an ATES
exon on its acceptor).

```{r barplot_novel_canonical, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=3.8}
novel_exon_counts <- ex_once[ex_once$novelTranscript] |>
  as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(site = factor(
    ifelse(canonical, "canonical (AG/GU)", "non-canonical"),
    levels = c("canonical (AG/GU)", "non-canonical")
  )) |>
  dplyr::count(site, .drop = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / sum(n)))

ggplot(novel_exon_counts, aes(x = site, y = n, fill = site)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("non-canonical"     = "#3A86FF",
                               "canonical (AG/GU)" = "grey70"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Novel event exons",
       subtitle = sprintf("n = %d exons\nATSS donors and ATES acceptors included",
                          sum(novel_exon_counts$n)),
       x = NULL, y = "Exons") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r noncanonical_list}
# the offenders: event exons whose acceptor is not AG or donor is not GU
noncanonical <- ex_once[!ex_once$canonical]

noncanonical |>
  as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::select(seqnames, start, end, strand, gene_id, tx_id,
                novelTranscript, exon_rank, event_type, acceptor, donor) |>
  dplyr::arrange(acceptor, donor) |>
  print(n = 20, width = Inf)
```

To eyeball one, read the whole exon with 5 intronic bases on each side, in
transcription order (`get_seq()` reverse-complements the minus strand). The
acceptor is the 2 intronic bases just before the exon (canonical `AG`), the
donor the 2 intronic bases just after it (canonical `GU`):

```{r inspect_one_noncanonical}
one <- noncanonical[1]

up5   <- get_seq(plyranges::flank_upstream(one,   width = 5), "hg38", as_rna = TRUE)
exon  <- get_seq(one,                                         "hg38", as_rna = TRUE)
down5 <- get_seq(plyranges::flank_downstream(one, width = 5), "hg38", as_rna = TRUE)

# intron(5) | EXON | intron(5), 5'->3'
cat(sprintf("%s | %s | %s\n", up5, exon, down5))

data.frame(
  intron_up_5   = as.character(up5),   # ...ends in AG for a canonical acceptor
  exon          = as.character(exon),
  intron_down_5 = as.character(down5)  # starts with GU for a canonical donor
)
```
